{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/mrava87/Desktop/OpenSource/pylops-agent-skills/plugins/pylops/skills/tune-regularization\n\nGoal: a **sweep script** in the user's project that evaluates a regularisation\nparameter over a range, applies one or more selection criteria, and reports the\nchosen value with a plot that justifies it. PyLops has no built-in L-curve / GCV /\ndiscrepancy helper, so the skill provides `reference/lcurve_template.py`.\n\nRequires a working inversion (operator passes the dot-test, solver runs). If there\nis none, use `solve-inverse-problem` first.\n\n## 0. Check the environment\n\nSame as the other PyLops skills: use the project's Python runner, check\n`pylops.__version__`, inspect solver signatures in the installed version.\n\n## 1. Identify the parameter(s)\n\nMap the user's solver to the knob being tuned and its meaning:\n\n| Solver | Parameter | Objective term |\n|---|---|---|\n| `cgls` / `lsqr` | `damp` | `damp² ‖x‖²` (for `lsqr` only with `x0=None`, see step 3) |\n| `regularized_inversion` | `epsRs=[ε₁, ε₂, …]` | `Σ εᵢ² ‖Rᵢ x‖²` |\n| `normal_equations_inversion` | `epsI`, `epsRs` (and `epsNRs`) | `epsI² ‖x‖²`, `Σ εᵢ² ‖Rᵢ x‖²` (same scaling as `regularized_inversion`) |\n| `ista` / `fista` | `eps` | `eps ‖SOpᴴ x‖₁` (effective threshold is `eps·alpha/2`) |\n| `splitbregman` | `epsRL1s`, `epsRL2s`, `mu` | L1 and L2 weights, data weight |\n| `spgl1` | `sigma` (BPDN) or `tau` (LASSO) | residual bound or L1-ball radius |\n| any Krylov solver without explicit regularisation | `niter` | early stopping (semi-convergence) |\n\nWith more than one weight, tune one at a time (fix the others at a\nscale-based guess), or fix their ratio and sweep an overall factor. Do not\nlaunch a full grid over several parameters unless the problem is small.\n\n## 2. Pick the criterion\n\nChoose based on what the user knows:\n\n1. **Known noise level** (sigma per sample, or an estimate from a noise-only\n   window): **discrepancy principle** - choose the largest regularisation whose\n   data residual `‖y − Op x‖` is ≤ `τ · σ · sqrt(N)`, `τ ≈ 1.0–1.1`. For\n   `spgl1`, this is exactly `sigma = τ σ sqrt(N)`.\n2. **Synthetic with a true model**: maximise `pylops.utils.metrics.snr(xtrue, x)`\n   (report it, but warn it does not transfer 1:1 to field data).\n3. **Nothing known**: **L-curve** - plot `log ‖Rx‖` vs `log ‖y − Op x‖` and pick the\n   point of maximum curvature. Needs a wide enough range to show both branches.\n4. **Small problem** (`Op.todense()` affordable, N, M ≲ 3000) and quadratic\n   regularisation: **GCV** computed exactly on the dense matrices (implemented in\n   the template).\n\nReport more than one criterion when they are cheap; disagreement between them is\ninformation for the user.\n\n## 3. Write and run the sweep\n\nAdapt `reference/lcurve_template.py`:\n\n- replace `build_problem` with the user's operator, data and regularisation;\n- replace `solve(eps, x0)` with the user's solver call **with everything else\n  fixed** (same `niter`, tolerance, `x0` policy);\n- use a **log-spaced grid** spanning at least 4 orders of magnitude around a\n  scale-based guess (e.g. `ε₀ ≈ ‖Opᴴ y‖ / ‖Rᴴ R Opᴴ y‖` for quadratic terms, or\n  `eps₀ ≈ max|Opᴴ y|` scale for L1 thresholds, where larger values give all-zero\n  models);\n- solve from large to small ε and **warm start** from the previous solution\n  (`x0=...`) to save iterations - unless the solver ignores `x0`. **Exception:\n  `damp` of `lsqr`** (PyLops and SciPy): with `x0` it solves for the correction\n  `x - x0`, so it penalises `damp² ‖x - x0‖²`, not `damp² ‖x‖²`, and a\n  warm-started sweep is biased (residual too low, discrepancy pick too large).\n  Use `x0=None` for every `lsqr(damp=...)` solve, or put the penalty in the\n  operator (`VStack([Op, eps*Reg])`, `regularized_inversion`), where `x0` is\n  safe. `cgls(damp=...)` and `epsRs` are not affected (checked numerically);\n- keep `niter` large enough that each solve has converged, otherwise the curve\n  measures iteration count, not regularisation (check a couple of cost curves);\n- for early stopping as regulariser, run once with a callback that stores\n  `x` every k iterations and compute the same criteria on iteration number.\n\nRun it, then look at the plot before trusting the automatic pick: an L-curve with\nno clear corner (common with L1 terms or very noisy data) should be reported as\nsuch, not forced. With derivative regularisers a second knee often appears at\nvery large ε (the model collapses into the null space of `R`, e.g. a linear\ntrend for `SecondDerivative`); it bends the other way and is not the L-curve\ncorner – the template's curvature orientation already excludes it.\n\n## 4. Hand off\n\nReport:\n\n- the parameter swept, the range and the number of solves;\n- the value picked by each criterion and the one recommended, with the reason;\n- the plot file(s) (L-curve, residual vs ε, SNR vs ε if available) and the\n  model at the chosen value next to one over- and one under-regularised model;\n- the exact line to change in the user's inversion script.\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"2e8cc56a-3de0-4ff1-9963-4a2831223d6c","uuid":"a9cb15f0-8317-4282-bb20-37e2b068ea37","timestamp":"2026-11-01T20:34:48.515Z","isSynthetic":true}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01PZv94DCTihH87ZErbymZ4p","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Template for choosing a regularisation weight in a PyLops inversion.\n\nRuns as-is on a toy 1-D deconvolution with second-derivative (smoothness)\nregularisation. To adapt it, replace ``build_problem`` and ``solve`` and keep\nthe sweep, the selection criteria and the plots.\n\nCriteria implemented:\n- L-curve corner (maximum curvature in log-log);\n- discrepancy principle (needs the noise standard deviation);\n- best SNR against a known model (synthetic tests only);\n- GCV, exact on dense matrices (small quadratic problems only).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\n\nimport pylops\nfrom pylops.utils.metrics import snr\n\n\ndef build_problem(rng):\n    \"\"\"ADAPT: return (Op, Reg, y, xtrue or None, noise_std or None).\"\"\"\n    nt = 201\n    t = np.arange(nt) * 0.004\n    h, _, hcenter = pylops.utils.wavelets.ricker(t[:41], f0=15)\n    Op = pylops.signalprocessing.Convolve1D(nt, h=h, offset=hcenter)\n    Reg = pylops.SecondDerivative(nt)\n\n    xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 3 * t) * np.exp(-t)  # smooth model\n    noise_std = 0.05\n    y = Op @ xtrue + noise_std * rng.standard_normal(nt)\n    return Op, Reg, y, xtrue, noise_std\n\n\ndef solve(Op, Reg, y, eps, x0):\n    \"\"\"ADAPT: the user's solver call with everything but ``eps`` fixed.\"\"\"\n    Opaug = pylops.VStack([Op, eps * Reg])\n    yaug = np.concatenate([y, np.zeros(Reg.shape[0])])\n    return pylops.cgls(Opaug, yaug, x0=x0, niter=200, tol=1e-10)[0]\n\n\ndef lcurve_corner(epsilons, rnorm, xnorm):\n    \"\"\"Index of the L-curve corner (maximum curvature in log-log).\n\n    Points are ordered by increasing eps so that the corner between the\n    \"under-regularised\" (vertical) and \"over-regularised\" (horizontal) branches\n    has positive curvature. A second knee with opposite curvature can appear\n    at very large eps (model pushed into the null space of the regulariser):\n    it is not the L-curve corner.\n    \"\"\"\n    order = np.argsort(epsilons)\n    lr, lx = np.log(rnorm[order]), np.log(xnorm[order])\n    # parametrise by arc length to make finite differences uniform\n    s = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(np.hypot(np.diff(lr), np.diff(lx)))])\n    dr, dx = np.gradient(lr, s), np.gradient(lx, s)\n    ddr, ddx = np.gradient(dr, s), np.gradient(dx, s)\n    kappa = (dr * ddx - ddr * dx) / (dr**2 + dx**2) ** 1.5\n    kappa[[0, -1]] = -np.inf  # ends are not valid corners\n    kappa_orig = np.empty_like(kappa)\n    kappa_orig[order] = kappa\n    return int(np.argmax(kappa_orig)), kappa_orig\n\n\ndef discrepancy(epsilons, rnorm, noise_std, n, tau=1.02):\n    \"\"\"Largest eps whose residual is below tau * noise level (None if none).\"\"\"\n    target = tau * noise_std * np.sqrt(n)\n    ok =

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
I recommend **`damp ≈ 0.25`**, chosen with the discrepancy principle. Your `damp=0.01` is about 25× too small, which is why the model looks noisy.

I wrote `sweep.py`, ran it, and it ends with `DAMP_CHOSEN=0.251`.

## How it was chosen
Because you know the noise standard deviation (σ = 0.1) exactly, the discrepancy principle is the right method. A correct model should fit the data only down to the noise level, ‖y − Kx‖ ≈ σ√N = 0.1·√120 ≈ 1.095, and no further. The script picks the **largest** `damp` whose residual is still at or below that level.

The script ran `lsqr` 51 times, with `damp` log-spaced from 1e-4 to 10, keeping `niter=2000` as you had it. I compared three of the solutions with the exact dense Tikhonov solution and they matched to within 1e-8 or better, so each solve had finished converging.

| Criterion | damp | ‖r‖ | SNR vs true model |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Discrepancy (σ known)** | **0.251** | 1.028 | 17.5 dB |
| Best SNR (only possible because this is synthetic) | 0.200 | 0.942 | 18.3 dB |
| GCV (exact, via SVD) | 0.100 | 0.864 | 15.2 dB |
| L-curve corner | 0.079 | 0.856 | 13.4 dB |
| Your `damp=0.01` | 0.010 | 0.832 | **−0.4 dB** |

- **Why 0.01 is noisy:** its residual is 0.83, only 0.76× the noise level. The solver is fitting the noise, and because K is a strong smoother, that noise gets amplified a lot in the model. The SNR is negative: the error is larger than the model itself.
- **The discrepancy pick is close to the best possible:** it lands next to the best-SNR value, which you could only compute because you know `xtrue`. On real data that check isn't available, but the noise-level argument still is.
- **GCV and the L-curve choose less damping:** they don't use the known σ, and here they slightly underfit the residual. Since you know σ, trust the discrepancy result over them.

## Change to make
```python
xinv = pylops.optimization.basic.lsqr(Op, y, damp=0.25, niter=2000)[0]
```

## Notes
- Every solve in the sweep starts from `x0=None` on purpose. If you pass a starting model, `lsqr` penalises the distance from that model, `damp²‖x − x0‖²`, rather than `damp²‖x‖²`. Warm-starting a sweep that way would bias the result.
- The plot is saved as `damp_sweep.png`. It shows the L-curve with each criterion's pick marked, residual and SNR against `damp` with the noise line, and the model at `damp=0.01`, at the chosen value, and at an over-damped value.

"""Choose the lsqr `damp` for a smoothing integral operator.

Primary criterion: discrepancy principle (noise std is known exactly, sigma=0.1):
pick the LARGEST damp whose residual ||y - K x|| <= tau * sigma * sqrt(N).
Also reported for comparison: L-curve corner, exact GCV (small dense problem)
and best SNR against the true model (synthetic only, not available on field data).

Note: every lsqr solve uses x0=None. With x0, lsqr penalises damp^2 ||x - x0||^2,
so a warm-started sweep would be biased.
"""

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

import pylops
from pylops.utils.metrics import snr

# ---------------- problem (as given by the user) ----------------
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
n = 120
s = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
K = np.exp(-((s[:, None] - s[None, :]) ** 2) / (2 * 0.04**2)) / n * 10
Op = pylops.MatrixMult(K)
xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2 * s) + 0.5 * (s > 0.6)
sigma = 0.1
y = Op @ xtrue + sigma * rng.standard_normal(n)

NITER = 2000
TAU = 1.0  # discrepancy safety factor (1.0-1.1)


def solve(damp):
    # x0=None on purpose (see module docstring); tight tolerances so each solve converges
    return pylops.optimization.basic.lsqr(
        Op, y, x0=None, damp=damp, niter=NITER, atol=1e-12, btol=1e-12
    )[0]


# ---------------- sweep ----------------
damps = np.logspace(1, -4, 51)  # large -> small, 5 orders of magnitude
xs = [solve(d) for d in damps]
rnorm = np.array([np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x) for x in xs])
xnorm = np.array([np.linalg.norm(x) for x in xs])
snrs = np.array([snr(xtrue, x) for x in xs])

# convergence check: compare to the exact dense Tikhonov solution at a few damps
for d in (damps[0], damps[len(damps) // 2], damps[-1]):
    xex = np.linalg.solve(K.T @ K + d**2 * np.eye(n), K.T @ y)
    xl = xs[list(damps).index(d)]
    print(f"convergence check damp={d:.1e}: rel.err vs exact = "
          f"{np.linalg.norm(xl - xex) / np.linalg.norm(xex):.1e}")

target = TAU * sigma * np.sqrt(n)
ok = np.where(rnorm <= target)[0]
i_disc = int(ok[np.argmax(damps[ok])]) if ok.size else None


# L-curve corner (max curvature in log-log, ordered by increasing damp)
def lcurve_corner(eps, r, x):
    order = np.argsort(eps)
    lr, lx = np.log(r[order]), np.log(x[order])
    t = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(np.hypot(np.diff(lr), np.diff(lx)))])
    dr, dx = np.gradient(lr, t), np.gradient(lx, t)
    ddr, ddx = np.gradient(dr, t), np.gradient(dx, t)
    kap = (dr * ddx - ddr * dx) / (dr**2 + dx**2) ** 1.5
    kap[[0, -1]] = -np.inf
    out = np.empty_like(kap)
    out[order] = kap
    return int(np.argmax(out))


i_lc = lcurve_corner(damps, rnorm, xnorm)

uty = U.T @ y
gcv = []
for d in damps:
    f = sv**2 / (sv**2 + d**2)  # filter factors
    res2 = np.sum(((1 - f) * uty) ** 2)  # K square -> no out-of-range component
    gcv.append(n * res2 / (n - f.sum()) ** 2)
gcv = np.array(gcv)
i_gcv = int(np.argmin(gcv))
i_snr = int(np.argmax(snrs))

# ---------------- report ----------------
print(f"\nSwept damp over [{damps.min():.0e}, {damps.max():.0e}], {len(damps)} solves")
print(f"noise level target tau*sigma*sqrt(N) = {target:.3f}")
picks = {"discrepancy": i_disc, "L-curve": i_lc, "GCV": i_gcv, "best SNR (synthetic)": i_snr}

i01 = int(np.argmin(np.abs(damps - 0.01)))
print(f"{'your damp=0.01':22s}: damp={damps[i01]:.3e}  ||r||={rnorm[i01]:.3f}  "

# ---------------- plots ----------------
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.5))

for name, i in picks.items():
    if i is not None:

"""Choose the lsqr `damp` for a smoothing integral operator.

Primary criterion: discrepancy principle (noise std is known exactly, sigma=0.1):
pick the LARGEST damp whose residual ||y - K x|| <= tau * sigma * sqrt(N).
Also reported for comparison: L-curve corner, exact GCV (small dense problem)
and best SNR against the true model (synthetic only, not available on field data).

Note: every lsqr solve uses x0=None. With x0, lsqr penalises damp^2 ||x - x0||^2,
so a warm-started sweep would be biased.
"""

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

import pylops
from pylops.utils.metrics import snr

# ---------------- problem (as given by the user) ----------------
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
n = 120
s = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
K = np.exp(-((s[:, None] - s[None, :]) ** 2) / (2 * 0.04**2)) / n * 10
Op = pylops.MatrixMult(K)
xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2 * s) + 0.5 * (s > 0.6)
sigma = 0.1
y = Op @ xtrue + sigma * rng.standard_normal(n)

NITER = 2000
TAU = 1.0  # discrepancy safety factor (1.0-1.1)


def solve(damp):
    # x0=None on purpose (see module docstring); tight tolerances so each solve converges
    return pylops.optimization.basic.lsqr(
        Op, y, x0=None, damp=damp, niter=NITER, atol=1e-12, btol=1e-12
    )[0]


# ---------------- sweep ----------------
damps = np.logspace(1, -4, 51)  # large -> small, 5 orders of magnitude
xs = [solve(d) for d in damps]
rnorm = np.array([np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x) for x in xs])
xnorm = np.array([np.linalg.norm(x) for x in xs])
snrs = np.array([snr(xtrue, x) for x in xs])

# convergence check: compare to the exact dense Tikhonov solution at a few damps
for d in (damps[0], damps[len(damps) // 2], damps[-1]):
    xex = np.linalg.solve(K.T @ K + d**2 * np.eye(n), K.T @ y)
    xl = xs[list(damps).index(d)]
    print(f"convergence check damp={d:.1e}: rel.err vs exact = "
          f"{np.linalg.norm(xl - xex) / np.linalg.norm(xex):.1e}")

# discrepancy principle
target = TAU * sigma * np.sqrt(n)
ok = np.where(rnorm <= target)[0]
i_disc = int(ok[np.argmax(damps[ok])]) if ok.size else None


# L-curve corner (max curvature in log-log, ordered by increasing damp)
def lcurve_corner(eps, r, x):
    order = np.argsort(eps)
    lr, lx = np.log(r[order]), np.log(x[order])
    t = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(np.hypot(np.diff(lr), np.diff(lx)))])
    dr, dx = np.gradient(lr, t), np.gradient(lx, t)
    ddr, ddx = np.gradient(dr, t), np.gradient(dx, t)
    kap = (dr * ddx - ddr * dx) / (dr**2 + dx**2) ** 1.5
    kap[[0, -1]] = -np.inf
    out = np.empty_like(kap)
    out[order] = kap
    return int(np.argmax(out))


i_lc = lcurve_corner(damps, rnorm, xnorm)

# exact GCV (dense, small problem)
U, sv, _ = np.linalg.svd(K)
uty = U.T @ y
gcv = []
for d in damps:
    f = sv**2 / (sv**2 + d**2)  # filter factors
    res2 = np.sum(((1 - f) * uty) ** 2)  # K square -> no out-of-range component
    gcv.append(n * res2 / (n - f.sum()) ** 2)
gcv = np.array(gcv)
i_gcv = int(np.argmin(gcv))
i_snr = int(np.argmax(snrs))

# ---------------- report ----------------
print(f"\nSwept damp over [{damps.min():.0e}, {damps.max():.0e}], {len(damps)} solves")
print(f"noise level target tau*sigma*sqrt(N) = {target:.3f}")
picks = {"discrepancy": i_disc, "L-curve": i_lc, "GCV": i_gcv, "best SNR (synthetic)": i_snr}
for name, i in picks.items():
    if i is None:
        print(f"{name:22s}: none (extend grid)")
        continue
    print(f"{name:22s}: damp={damps[i]:.3e}  ||r||={rnorm[i]:.3f}  SNR={snrs[i]:.2f} dB")
i01 = int(np.argmin(np.abs(damps - 0.01)))
print(f"{'your damp=0.01':22s}: damp={damps[i01]:.3e}  ||r||={rnorm[i01]:.3f}  "
      f"SNR={snrs[i01]:.2f} dB  (residual {rnorm[i01] / (sigma * np.sqrt(n)):.2f}x noise -> overfitting)")

# ---------------- plots ----------------
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.5))
axs[0].loglog(rnorm, xnorm, ".-k")
for name, i in picks.items():
    if i is not None:
        axs[0].loglog(rnorm[i], xnorm[i], "o", label=name)
axs[0].axvline(target, color="r", ls="--", lw=0.8)
axs[0].set(xlabel="||y - Kx||", ylabel="||x||", title="L-curve")
axs[0].legend(fontsize=8)

axs[1].loglog(damps, rnorm, ".-k", label="||r||")
axs[1].axhline(target, color="r", ls="--", label="sigma*sqrt(N)")
if i_disc is not None:
    axs[1].axvline(damps[i_disc], color="g", ls=":", label="discrepancy pick")
ax2 = axs[1].twinx()
ax2.semilogx(damps, snrs, ".-b")
ax2.set_ylabel("SNR [dB]", color="b")
axs[1].set(xlabel="damp", title="residual and SNR vs damp")
axs[1].legend(fontsize=8, loc="lower right")

ichosen = i_disc if i_disc is not None else i_gcv
axs[2].plot(s, xtrue, "k", lw=2, label="true")
axs[2].plot(s, xs[i01], lw=0.8, label="damp=0.01 (under-reg.)")
axs[2].plot(s, xs[ichosen], lw=1.5, label=f"chosen damp={damps[ichosen]:.3g}")
axs[2].plot(s, xs[max(0, ichosen - 8)], lw=1, label=f"over-reg. damp={damps[max(0, ichosen - 8)]:.3g}")
axs[2].set_ylim(-2.5, 2.5)
axs[2].legend(fontsize=8)
axs[2].set_title("models")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("damp_sweep.png", dpi=120)
print("plot saved to damp_sweep.png")

damp_chosen = float(f"{damps[ichosen]:.3g}")
print(f"DAMP_CHOSEN={damp_chosen}")

To adapt it, replace ``build_problem`` and ``solve`` and keep\nthe sweep, the selection criteria and the plots.\n\nCriteria implemented:\n- L-curve corner (maximum curvature in log-log);\n- discrepancy principle (needs the noise standard deviation);\n- best SNR against a known model (synthetic tests only);\n- GCV, exact on dense matrices (small quadratic problems only).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\n\nimport pylops\nfrom pylops.utils.metrics import snr\n\n\ndef build_problem(rng):\n    \"\"\"ADAPT: return (Op, Reg, y, xtrue or None, noise_std or None).\"\"\"\n    nt = 201\n    t = np.arange(nt) * 0.004\n    h, _, hcenter = pylops.utils.wavelets.ricker(t[:41], f0=15)\n    Op = pylops.signalprocessing.Convolve1D(nt, h=h, offset=hcenter)\n    Reg = pylops.SecondDerivative(nt)\n\n    xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 3 * t) * np.exp(-t)  # smooth model\n    noise_std = 0.05\n    y = Op @ xtrue + noise_std * rng.standard_normal(nt)\n    return Op, Reg, y, xtrue, noise_std\n\n\ndef solve(Op, Reg, y, eps, x0):\n    \"\"\"ADAPT: the user's solver call with everything but ``eps`` fixed.\"\"\"\n    Opaug = pylops.VStack([Op, eps * Reg])\n    yaug = np.concatenate([y, np.zeros(Reg.shape[0])])\n    return pylops.cgls(Opaug, yaug, x0=x0, niter=200, tol=1e-10)[0]\n\n\ndef lcurve_corner(epsilons, rnorm, xnorm):\n    \"\"\"Index of the L-curve corner (maximum curvature in log-log).\n\n    Points are ordered by increasing eps so that the corner between the\n    \"under-regularised\" (vertical) and \"over-regularised\" (horizontal) branches\n    has positive curvature. A second knee with opposite curvature can appear\n    at very large eps (model pushed into the null space of the regulariser):\n    it is not the L-curve corner.\n    \"\"\"\n    order = np.argsort(epsilons)\n    lr, lx = np.log(rnorm[order]), np.log(xnorm[order])\n    # parametrise by arc length to make finite differences uniform\n    s = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(np.hypot(np.diff(lr), np.diff(lx)))])\n    dr, dx = np.gradient(lr, s), np.gradient(lx, s)\n    ddr, ddx = np.gradient(dr, s), np.gradient(dx, s)\n    kappa = (dr * ddx - ddr * dx) / (dr**2 + dx**2) ** 1.5\n    kappa[[0, -1]] = -np.inf  # ends are not valid corners\n    kappa_orig = np.empty_like(kappa)\n    kappa_orig[order] = kappa\n    return int(np.argmax(kappa_orig)), kappa_orig\n\n\ndef discrepancy(epsilons, rnorm, noise_std, n, tau=1.02):\n    \"\"\"Largest eps whose residual is below tau * noise level (None if none).\"\"\"\n    target = tau * noise_std * np.sqrt(n)\n    ok = np.where(rnorm <= target)[0]\n    return (int(ok[np.argmax(epsilons[ok])]) if ok.size else None), target\n\n\ndef gcv_dense(Op, Reg, y, epsilons):\n    \"\"\"Exact GCV for min ||y - A x||^2 + eps^2 ||R x||^2 (small problems).\"\"\"\n    A, R = Op.todense(), Reg.todense()\n    AtA, RtR, n = A.T.conj() @ A, R.T.conj() @ R, A.shape[0]\n    g = []\n    for eps in epsilons:\n        H = A @ np.linalg.solve(AtA + eps**2 * RtR, A.T.conj())  # influence matrix\n        r = y - H @ y\n        g.append(n * np.real(r.conj() @ r) / np.real(n - np.trace(H)) ** 2)\n    return int(np.argmin(g)), np.array(g)\n\n\ndef main(neps=25, seed=0, dense_gcv=True):\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    Op, Reg, y, xtrue, noise_std = build_problem(rng)\n\n    # log grid around a scale-based guess, solved from large to small eps\n    eps0 = np.linalg.norm(Op.H @ y) / np.linalg.norm(Reg.H @ (Reg @ (Op.H @ y)))\n    epsilons = eps0 * np.logspace(3, -3, neps)\n\n    xs, rnorm, xnorm = [], [], []\n    x0 = np.zeros(Op.shape[1], dtype=Op.dtype)\n    for eps in epsilons:\n        x = solve(Op, Reg, y, eps, x0)\n        x0 = x  # warm start\n        xs.append(x)\n        rnorm.append(np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x))\n        xnorm.append(np.linalg.norm(Reg @ x))\n    rnorm, xnorm = np.array(rnorm), np.array(xnorm)\n\n    picks = {}\n    icorner, _ = lcurve_corner(epsilons, rnorm, xnorm)\n    picks[\"L-curve\"] = icorner\n    if noise_std is not None:\n        idisc, target = discrepancy(epsilons, rnorm, noise_std, y.size)\n        if idisc is None:\n            print(f\"discrepancy: no eps reaches residual {target:.3e}; extend the grid\")\n        else:\n            picks[\"discrepancy\"] = idisc\n    snrs = None\n    if xtrue is not None:\n        snrs = np.array([snr(xtrue, x) for x in xs])\n        picks[\

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
I chose **`damp ≈ 0.28`** using the discrepancy principle. At that value the inverted model is about 16.8 dB SNR against the true model; at your `damp=0.01` it was −0.4 dB, which means the result was mostly amplified noise.

**Why the discrepancy principle:** you know σ = 0.1 exactly, and that is the case this rule is designed for. If the model explained the data perfectly, the remaining misfit would be just the noise, so `‖y − Op x‖` should be about σ·√N = 0.1·√120 ≈ 1.095. A smaller misfit means the model is fitting noise. The rule picks the largest damping that still brings the misfit down to that level.

With `damp=0.01` your misfit was 0.83, about 24% below the noise level, so the model was fitting noise. That's expected here: the singular values of K run from about 1 down to about 1e-19, so with weak damping the small ones blow the noise up.

**What `sweep.py` does:**
- It solves for 61 values of `damp`, log-spaced from 1e1 down to 1e-5, using your `lsqr` call unchanged. It then refines the discrepancy pick by bisection.
- Every solve starts from `x0=None`. If you start PyLops `lsqr` from a previous solution, it penalises `damp²‖x − x0‖²` instead of `damp²‖x‖²`, which would bias the sweep.
- Each solve has fully converged: it matches an exact dense solve to within about 1e-10 relative error.
- It compares the pick with three other ways of choosing `damp`:

| criterion | damp | misfit / noise level | SNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| your value | 0.01 | 0.76 | −0.4 |
| **discrepancy (chosen)** | **0.281** | **1.00** | **16.8** |
| L-curve corner | 0.079 | 0.78 | 13.4 |
| GCV | 0.10 | 0.79 | 15.2 |
| best SNR (uses the true model) | 0.20 | 0.86 | 18.3 |

All three criteria that don't need the true model put the best value between 0.08 and 0.3, one to one and a half orders of magnitude above 0.01. The best possible value, 0.20, only exists because this is a synthetic test, so don't use it for real data. The discrepancy pick is slightly on the smooth side of it: the jump at s = 0.6 comes out a little rounded. That's usual, because with a fixed noise level this rule tends to over-smooth a bit. If you would rather keep more detail, use 0.1 (the GCV pick); it's also safe.

The plot is in `damp_sweep.png`. It shows the L-curve, misfit and SNR against `damp`, and the models at the chosen value, at 10× that value (too smooth), and at your 0.01.

**Change in your script:**
```python
xinv = pylops.optimization.basic.lsqr(Op, y, damp=0.28, niter=2000)[0]
```

The script ends by printing `DAMP_CHOSEN=0.2809`.

"""Choose `damp` for lsqr on a smoothing-kernel inversion.

Primary criterion: discrepancy principle (noise std is known exactly = 0.1).
Also reported for comparison: L-curve corner, exact GCV (problem is small),
and best SNR against the true model (synthetic only - not available on field data).

Note: every lsqr solve uses x0=None. With x0, PyLops/SciPy lsqr penalise
damp^2 ||x - x0||^2 instead of damp^2 ||x||^2, which biases a warm-started sweep.
"""

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

import pylops
from pylops.utils.metrics import snr

# ---------------- problem (exactly as given) ----------------
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
n = 120
s = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
K = np.exp(-((s[:, None] - s[None, :]) ** 2) / (2 * 0.04 ** 2)) / n * 10
Op = pylops.MatrixMult(K)
xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2 * s) + 0.5 * (s > 0.6)
sigma = 0.1
y = Op @ xtrue + sigma * rng.standard_normal(n)
N = y.size

# sanity: adjoint
pylops.utils.dottest(Op, n, n, raiseerror=True)


def solve(damp):
    # fixed settings for all solves; x0=None on purpose (see docstring)
    return pylops.optimization.basic.lsqr(
        Op, y, x0=None, damp=damp, niter=2000, atol=1e-12, btol=1e-12, conlim=1e12
    )[0]


# ---------------- sweep ----------------
svals = np.linalg.svd(K, compute_uv=False)
print(f"singular values of K: max={svals[0]:.3e}, min={svals[-1]:.3e}")
damps = np.logspace(1, -5, 61)  # large -> small, spans 6 decades around ||K||
xs, rnorm, xnorm = [], [], []
for d in damps:
    x = solve(d)
    xs.append(x)
    rnorm.append(np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x))
    xnorm.append(np.linalg.norm(x))
xs, rnorm, xnorm = np.array(xs), np.array(rnorm), np.array(xnorm)
snrs = np.array([snr(xtrue, x) for x in xs])

# convergence check: compare a couple of lsqr solutions with the exact Tikhonov solution
for d in (1e-1, 1e-3):
    xex = np.linalg.solve(K.T @ K + d**2 * np.eye(n), K.T @ y)
    print(f"convergence check damp={d:.0e}: rel. err vs dense solve = "
          f"{np.linalg.norm(solve(d) - xex) / np.linalg.norm(xex):.1e}")

# ---------------- criteria ----------------
# 1) discrepancy principle: largest damp with ||r|| <= tau * sigma * sqrt(N)
tau = 1.0
target = tau * sigma * np.sqrt(N)
ok = np.where(rnorm <= target)[0]
idisc = int(ok[np.argmax(damps[ok])])
# refine by bisection in log(damp) between the bracketing grid points
lo, hi = np.log10(damps[idisc]), np.log10(damps[idisc - 1])
for _ in range(40):
    mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    if np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ solve(10**mid)) <= target:
        lo = mid
    else:
        hi = mid
damp_disc = 10**lo
x_disc = solve(damp_disc)

# 2) L-curve corner (max curvature in log-log, ordered by increasing damp)
order = np.argsort(damps)
lr, lx = np.log(rnorm[order]), np.log(xnorm[order])
sarc = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(np.hypot(np.diff(lr), np.diff(lx)))])
dr, dx = np.gradient(lr, sarc), np.gradient(lx, sarc)
ddr, ddx = np.gradient(dr, sarc), np.gradient(dx, sarc)
kappa = (dr * ddx - ddr * dx) / (dr**2 + dx**2) ** 1.5
kappa[[0, -1]] = -np.inf
icorner = int(order[np.argmax(kappa)])

# 3) exact GCV
AtA = K.T @ K
gcv = []
for d in damps:
    H = K @ np.linalg.solve(AtA + d**2 * np.eye(n), K.T)
    r = y - H @ y
    gcv.append(N * (r @ r) / (N - np.trace(H)) ** 2)
gcv = np.array(gcv)
igcv = int(np.argmin(gcv))

# 4) best SNR (oracle, synthetic only)
isnr = int(np.argmax(snrs))

x_user = solve(0.01)
print(f"\nnoise level target sigma*sqrt(N) = {target:.4f}")
print(f"{'criterion':14s} {'damp':>10s} {'||r||':>9s} {'||r||/(s*sqrtN)':>16s} {'SNR[dB]':>8s}")
rows = [("user (0.01)", 0.01, x_user),
        ("discrepancy", damp_disc, x_disc),
        ("L-curve", damps[icorner], xs[icorner]),
        ("GCV", damps[igcv], xs[igcv]),
        ("best SNR*", damps[isnr], xs[isnr])]
for name, d, x in rows:
    r = np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x)
    print(f"{name:14s} {d:10.3e} {r:9.4f} {r / target:16.3f} {snr(xtrue, x):8.2f}")
print("* oracle: uses xtrue, not available on real data")

# ---------------- plots ----------------
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.5))
axs[0].loglog(rnorm, xnorm, ".-k")
for name, i in [("L-curve", icorner), ("GCV", igcv), ("best SNR", isnr)]:
    axs[0].loglog(rnorm[i], xnorm[i], "o", label=name)
axs[0].loglog(np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x_disc), np.linalg.norm(x_disc), "*", ms=12,
              label="discrepancy")
axs[0].axvline(target, color="r", ls="--", lw=0.8)
axs[0].set(xlabel="||y - Op x||", ylabel="||x||", title="L-curve")
axs[0].legend()

axs[1].loglog(damps, rnorm, ".-k", label="||r||")
axs[1].axhline(target, color="r", ls="--", label="sigma*sqrt(N)")
axs[1].axvline(damp_disc, color="r", ls=":")
axs[1].set(xlabel="damp", ylabel="||r||")
axs[1].legend(loc="upper left")
ax2 = axs[1].twinx()
ax2.semilogx(damps, snrs, ".-b")
ax2.set_ylabel("SNR [dB]", color="b")
axs[1].set_title("Residual and SNR vs damp")

axs[2].plot(s, xtrue, "k", lw=2, label="true")
axs[2].plot(s, solve(10 * damp_disc), label=f"over (damp={10*damp_disc:.2g})")
axs[2].plot(s, x_disc, lw=2, label=f"chosen (damp={damp_disc:.3g})")
axs[2].plot(s, x_user, alpha=0.6, label="user (damp=0.01)")
axs[2].set_ylim(-3, 3)
axs[2].legend(fontsize=8)
axs[2].set_title("Models")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("damp_sweep.png", dpi=120)
print("plot saved to damp_sweep.png")

print(f"DAMP_CHOSEN={damp_disc:.4g}")

To adapt it, replace ``build_problem`` and ``solve`` and keep\nthe sweep, the selection criteria and the plots.\n\nCriteria implemented:\n- L-curve corner (maximum curvature in log-log);\n- discrepancy principle (needs the noise standard deviation);\n- best SNR against a known model (synthetic tests only);\n- GCV, exact on dense matrices (small quadratic problems only).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\n\nimport pylops\nfrom pylops.utils.metrics import snr\n\n\ndef build_problem(rng):\n    \"\"\"ADAPT: return (Op, Reg, y, xtrue or None, noise_std or None).\"\"\"\n    nt = 201\n    t = np.arange(nt) * 0.004\n    h, _, hcenter = pylops.utils.wavelets.ricker(t[:41], f0=15)\n    Op = pylops.signalprocessing.Convolve1D(nt, h=h, offset=hcenter)\n    Reg = pylops.SecondDerivative(nt)\n\n    xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 3 * t) * np.exp(-t)  # smooth model\n    noise_std = 0.05\n    y = Op @ xtrue + noise_std * rng.standard_normal(nt)\n    return Op, Reg, y, xtrue, noise_std\n\n\ndef solve(Op, Reg, y, eps, x0):\n    \"\"\"ADAPT: the user's solver call with everything but ``eps`` fixed.\"\"\"\n    Opaug = pylops.VStack([Op, eps * Reg])\n    yaug = np.concatenate([y, np.zeros(Reg.shape[0])])\n    return pylops.cgls(Opaug, yaug, x0=x0, niter=200, tol=1e-10)[0]\n\n\ndef lcurve_corner(epsilons, rnorm, xnorm):\n    \"\"\"Index of the L-curve corner (maximum curvature in log-log).\n\n    Points are ordered by increasing eps so that the corner between the\n    \"under-regularised\" (vertical) and \"over-regularised\" (horizontal) branches\n    has positive curvature. A second knee with opposite curvature can appear\n    at very large eps (model pushed into the null space of the regulariser):\n    it is not the L-curve corner.\n    \"\"\"\n    order = np.argsort(epsilons)\n    lr, lx = np.log(rnorm[order]), np.log(xnorm[order])\n    # parametrise by arc length to make finite differences uniform\n    s = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(np.hypot(np.diff(lr), np.diff(lx)))])\n    dr, dx = np.gradient(lr, s), np.gradient(lx, s)\n    ddr, ddx = np.gradient(dr, s), np.gradient(dx, s)\n    kappa = (dr * ddx - ddr * dx) / (dr**2 + dx**2) ** 1.5\n    kappa[[0, -1]] = -np.inf  # ends are not valid corners\n    kappa_orig = np.empty_like(kappa)\n    kappa_orig[order] = kappa\n    return int(np.argmax(kappa_orig)), kappa_orig\n\n\ndef discrepancy(epsilons, rnorm, noise_std, n, tau=1.02):\n    \"\"\"Largest eps whose residual is below tau * noise level (None if none).\"\"\"\n    target = tau * noise_std * np.sqrt(n)\n    ok = np.where(rnorm <= target)[0]\n    return (int(ok[np.argmax(epsilons[ok])]) if ok.size else None), target\n\n\ndef gcv_dense(Op, Reg, y, epsilons):\n    \"\"\"Exact GCV for min ||y - A x||^2 + eps^2 ||R x||^2 (small problems).\"\"\"\n    A, R = Op.todense(), Reg.todense()\n    AtA, RtR, n = A.T.conj() @ A, R.T.conj() @ R, A.shape[0]\n    g = []\n    for eps in epsilons:\n        H = A @ np.linalg.solve(AtA + eps**2 * RtR, A.T.conj())  # influence matrix\n        r = y - H @ y\n        g.append(n * np.real(r.conj() @ r) / np.real(n - np.trace(H)) ** 2)\n    return int(np.argmin(g)), np.array(g)\n\n\ndef main(neps=25, seed=0, dense_gcv=True):\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    Op, Reg, y, xtrue, noise_std = build_problem(rng)\n\n    # log grid around a scale-based guess, solved from large to small eps\n    eps0 = np.linalg.norm(Op.H @ y) / np.linalg.norm(Reg.H @ (Reg @ (Op.H @ y)))\n    epsilons = eps0 * np.logspace(3, -3, neps)\n\n    xs, rnorm, xnorm = [], [], []\n    x0 = np.zeros(Op.shape[1], dtype=Op.dtype)\n    for eps in epsilons:\n        x = solve(Op, Reg, y, eps, x0)\n        x0 = x  # warm start\n        xs.append(x)\n        rnorm.append(np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x))\n        xnorm.append(np.linalg.norm(Reg @ x))\n    rnorm, xnorm = np.array(rnorm), np.array(xnorm)\n\n    picks = {}\n    icorner, _ = lcurve_corner(epsilons, rnorm, xnorm)\n    picks[\"L-curve\"] = icorner\n    if noise_std is not None:\n        idisc, target = discrepancy(epsilons, rnorm, noise_std, y.size)\n        if idisc is None:\n            print(f\"discrepancy: no eps reaches residual {target:.3e}; extend the grid\")\n        else:\n            picks[\"discrepancy\"] = idisc\n    snrs = None\n    if xtrue is not None:\n        snrs = np.array([snr(xtrue, x) for x in xs])\n        pic

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
I wrote `sweep.py` and ran it. It recommends **`damp ≈ 0.28`**, which is about 28× larger than your 0.01. The last line it prints is `DAMP_CHOSEN=0.2809`.

**How I chose it: the discrepancy principle.** `lsqr` with `damp` minimises ‖y − Kx‖² + damp²‖x‖². Because you know the noise is white with σ = 0.1, the noise vector should have norm about σ√n = 0.1·√120 ≈ **1.095**. A good solution should fit the data only that closely:

- If the residual is below 1.095, the solver is fitting noise.
- If it is above 1.095, the solution is over-smoothed.

The residual only goes up as `damp` increases, so the script tries 26 values from 1e-4 to 10 on a log scale. It then narrows down by bisection to the `damp` where the residual equals 1.095.

**Why your result looked noisy.** With `damp=0.01` the residual is 0.83, well below the noise level. Your kernel is a narrow Gaussian blur, and its small singular values are being divided into the noise, so it gets amplified. You can see it in the size of the solution: ‖x‖ is 11.6 against about 7.3 at the chosen damp. The error relative to `xtrue` is 105%, which means the result is mostly noise.

The script uses `xtrue` only to print the error column, as a check; it plays no part in the choice. The chosen value comes out close to the best possible one, which you could only find if you knew the true model. The discrepancy principle tends to over-smooth slightly, and that's the gap you see here.

- `damp` penalises the size of x, so it shrinks the step at s = 0.6 and the sine wave toward zero. If you want to keep edges or smoothness, consider regularising with a derivative operator instead, such as `pylops.optimization.leastsquares.regularized_inversion` with `pylops.SecondDerivative`. You can pick its weight by the same discrepancy rule.

"""Choose the lsqr damping via Morozov's discrepancy principle.

lsqr with `damp` solves   min_x ||y - K x||_2^2 + damp^2 ||x||_2^2.
With known white noise of std sigma, the expected noise norm is
sigma * sqrt(n). We pick the damp whose data residual matches it:
    ||y - K x(damp)||_2 = tau * sigma * sqrt(n),   tau = 1.
The residual increases monotonically with damp, so we sweep a log grid,
then refine the crossing by bisection in log(damp).
"""
import numpy as np
import pylops

# ---- synthetic problem (as given) -----------------------------------------
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
n = 120
s = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
K = np.exp(-((s[:, None] - s[None, :]) ** 2) / (2 * 0.04 ** 2)) / n * 10
Op = pylops.MatrixMult(K)
xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2 * s) + 0.5 * (s > 0.6)
sigma = 0.1
y = Op @ xtrue + sigma * rng.standard_normal(n)

target = 1.0 * sigma * np.sqrt(n)  # tau = 1


def solve(damp):
    return pylops.optimization.basic.lsqr(Op, y, damp=damp, niter=2000)[0]


def resnorm(damp):
    return np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ solve(damp))


# ---- coarse log sweep -----------------------------------------------------
damps = np.logspace(-4, 1, 26)
print(f"target residual  sigma*sqrt(n) = {target:.4f}")
print(f"{'damp':>10} {'||y-Kx||':>10} {'||x||':>10} {'rel.err*':>10}")
res = []
for d in damps:
    x = solve(d)
    r = np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x)
    res.append(r)
    err = np.linalg.norm(x - xtrue) / np.linalg.norm(xtrue)
    print(f"{d:10.2e} {r:10.4f} {np.linalg.norm(x):10.3f} {err:10.4f}")
res = np.array(res)
print("* rel.err uses xtrue: diagnostic only, NOT used for the choice")

# ---- refine crossing by bisection in log(damp) ----------------------------
i = np.argmax(res >= target)
if i == 0 or res[i] < target:
    raise RuntimeError("discrepancy target not bracketed by the sweep")
lo, hi = np.log10(damps[i - 1]), np.log10(damps[i])
for _ in range(40):
    mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    if resnorm(10 ** mid) < target:
        lo = mid
    else:
        hi = mid
damp_chosen = 10 ** (0.5 * (lo + hi))

x_dp = solve(damp_chosen)
x_old = solve(0.01)
rel = lambda x: np.linalg.norm(x - xtrue) / np.linalg.norm(xtrue)
print(f"\ndamp=0.01   : residual={np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x_old):.4f}  rel.err={rel(x_old):.4f}")
print(f"damp(DP)    : residual={np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x_dp):.4f}  rel.err={rel(x_dp):.4f}")
print(f"DAMP_CHOSEN={damp_chosen:.4g}")

"""Choose the lsqr damping via Morozov's discrepancy principle.

With known white noise of std sigma, the expected noise norm is
sigma * sqrt(n). We pick the damp whose data residual matches it:

The residual increases monotonically with damp, so we sweep a log grid,

"""
import numpy as np
import pylops

# ---- synthetic problem (as given) -----------------------------------------
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
n = 120
s = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
K = np.exp(-((s[:, None] - s[None, :]) ** 2) / (2 * 0.04 ** 2)) / n * 10

xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2 * s) + 0.5 * (s > 0.6)
sigma = 0.1
y = Op @ xtrue + sigma * rng.standard_normal(n)

target = 1.0 * sigma * np.sqrt(n)  # tau = 1


def solve(damp):
    return pylops.optimization.basic.lsqr(Op, y, damp=damp, niter=2000)[0]


def resnorm(damp):
    return np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ solve(damp))


# ---- coarse log sweep -----------------------------------------------------
damps = np.logspace(-4, 1, 26)
print(f"target residual  sigma*sqrt(n) = {target:.4f}")
print(f"{'damp':>10} {'||y-Kx||':>10} {'||x||':>10} {'rel.err*':>10}")
res = []
for d in damps:
    x = solve(d)
    r = np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x)
    res.append(r)
    err = np.linalg.norm(x - xtrue) / np.linalg.norm(xtrue)

res = np.array(res)
print("* rel.err uses xtrue: diagnostic only, NOT used for the choice")

lo, hi = np.log10(damps[i - 1]), np.log10(damps[i])
for _ in range(40):
    mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    if resnorm(10 ** mid) < target:
        lo = mid
    else:
        hi = mid
damp_chosen = 10 ** (0.5 * (lo + hi))

x_dp = solve(damp_chosen)
x_old = solve(0.01)
rel = lambda x: np.linalg.norm(x - xtrue) / np.linalg.norm(xtrue)
print(f"\ndamp=0.01   : residual={np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x_old):.4f}  rel.err={rel(x_old):.4f}")
print(f"damp(DP)    : residual={np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x_dp):.4f}  rel.err={rel(x_dp):.4f}")

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
I recommend **`damp ≈ 0.28`**. I wrote `sweep.py`, ran it, and its last line is `DAMP_CHOSEN=0.2809`.

**Method: the discrepancy principle.** Because you know the noise level, you can choose `damp` without trial and error. pylops' `lsqr` minimizes `||y − Kx||² + damp²·||x||²`. If the model fits the data more closely than the noise level, it is fitting noise. If it fits less closely, it is over-smoothed. So the rule is to pick the `damp` where the residual matches the noise:

  `||y − K x_damp||₂ = τ·σ·√n = 1.0 × 0.1 × √120 ≈ 1.095`

The residual always increases as `damp` increases, so there is exactly one such value. The script runs `lsqr` for 26 values of `damp` from 1e‑4 to 10, spaced evenly on a log scale. It then narrows down the crossing point by repeated halving (bisection).

**Results:**

| damp | residual / target | relative error vs xtrue |
|---|---|---|
| 0.01 (your choice) | 0.76 | **1.05** (the error is as large as the signal itself) |
| **0.281 (discrepancy)** | **1.00** | **0.144** |
| best on the grid (≈0.16) | 0.82 | 0.126 |

- At `damp=0.01` the residual is well below the noise level, which confirms the model is fitting noise. Raising `damp` to 0.28 cuts the error by about 7×.
- `xtrue` is used only for the report. It played no part in choosing `damp`, so the method works on real data where `xtrue` is unknown. The value it picks is close to the best one on the grid. It errs a little toward over-smoothing, which is typical for this method.
- I compared the `lsqr` solution at the chosen `damp` with an exact solution computed via SVD. They match to about 1e‑12, so the 2000 iterations are enough and the residuals in the table are reliable.

**Practical notes:**
- If you're unsure about σ, people often use a safety factor of τ ≈ 1.0–1.1. A larger τ gives a smoother model.
- Another source of noise in your current setup: with plain `damp`, the solver also runs to near-convergence. Stopping `lsqr` early has its own regularizing effect. Choosing `damp` this way removes your dependence on that.
- If the step at s=0.6 matters to you, consider penalizing a derivative instead of `||x||`. For a sharp step, total variation is the usual choice. In pylops you would use `RegularizedInversion` with a `FirstDerivative` operator. The same discrepancy rule then sets its weight.

"""Choose the lsqr damping parameter with Morozov's discrepancy principle.

pylops' lsqr with `damp` solves   min ||y - Op x||^2 + damp^2 ||x||^2.
With known noise std sigma, the residual of a good solution should be about as
large as the noise itself: ||y - Op x||_2 ~= tau * sigma * sqrt(n) (tau ~ 1).
Smaller residual => fitting noise (under-regularized); larger => over-smoothed.
The residual grows monotonically with damp, so we sweep damp on a log grid and
pick the value where the residual crosses the target (refined by bisection).
"""
import numpy as np
import pylops

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
n = 120
s = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
K = np.exp(-((s[:, None] - s[None, :]) ** 2) / (2 * 0.04 ** 2)) / n * 10
Op = pylops.MatrixMult(K)
xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2 * s) + 0.5 * (s > 0.6)
y = Op @ xtrue + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(n)

sigma = 0.1
tau = 1.0
target = tau * sigma * np.sqrt(n)
NITER = 2000


def solve(damp):
    x = pylops.optimization.basic.lsqr(Op, y, damp=damp, niter=NITER,
                                       atol=1e-12, btol=1e-12)[0]
    return x, np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x)


def rel_err(x):
    return np.linalg.norm(x - xtrue) / np.linalg.norm(xtrue)


# --- 1) coarse log sweep -----------------------------------------------------
damps = np.logspace(-4, 1, 26)
res = []
print(f"target residual  tau*sigma*sqrt(n) = {target:.4f}")
print(f"{'damp':>10s} {'||r||':>10s} {'||r||/target':>13s} {'relerr(info)':>13s}")
for d in damps:
    x, r = solve(d)
    res.append(r)
    print(f"{d:10.2e} {r:10.4f} {r / target:13.3f} {rel_err(x):13.3f}")
res = np.array(res)

# --- 2) bracket the crossing and refine by bisection in log(damp) ------------
idx = np.where((res[:-1] - target) * (res[1:] - target) <= 0)[0]
if len(idx) == 0:
    raise RuntimeError("Target residual not bracketed; widen the damp range.")
lo, hi = np.log10(damps[idx[0]]), np.log10(damps[idx[0] + 1])
for _ in range(40):
    mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    _, r = solve(10 ** mid)
    if r < target:
        lo = mid
    else:
        hi = mid
damp_dp = 10 ** (0.5 * (lo + hi))
x_dp, r_dp = solve(damp_dp)

# --- 3) sanity check against the exact Tikhonov solution via SVD ------------
U, S, Vt = np.linalg.svd(K)
x_svd = Vt.T @ (S / (S ** 2 + damp_dp ** 2) * (U.T @ y))
x_old, r_old = solve(0.01)

print()
print(f"discrepancy damp           = {damp_dp:.4g}")
print(f"residual at chosen damp    = {r_dp:.4f} (target {target:.4f})")
print(f"lsqr vs exact SVD mismatch = "
      f"{np.linalg.norm(x_dp - x_svd) / np.linalg.norm(x_svd):.2e}")
print(f"damp=0.01   : ||r||={r_old:.4f} ({r_old / target:.2f}x target), "
      f"relerr={rel_err(x_old):.3f}")
print(f"damp={damp_dp:.3g}: ||r||={r_dp:.4f} ({r_dp / target:.2f}x target), "
      f"relerr={rel_err(x_dp):.3f}")
# (relerr uses xtrue and is only reported for information; it was NOT used
#  to select damp, since xtrue is unknown in a real problem.)
print(f"DAMP_CHOSEN={damp_dp:.4g}")

"""Choose the lsqr damping parameter with Morozov's discrepancy principle.

pylops' lsqr with `damp` solves   min ||y - Op x||^2 + damp^2 ||x||^2.
With known noise std sigma, the residual of a good solution should be about as
large as the noise itself: ||y - Op x||_2 ~= tau * sigma * sqrt(n) (tau ~ 1).
Smaller residual => fitting noise (under-regularized); larger => over-smoothed.
The residual grows monotonically with damp, so we sweep damp on a log grid and
pick the value where the residual crosses the target (refined by bisection).
"""
import numpy as np
import pylops

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
n = 120
s = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
K = np.exp(-((s[:, None] - s[None, :]) ** 2) / (2 * 0.04 ** 2)) / n * 10
Op = pylops.MatrixMult(K)
xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2 * s) + 0.5 * (s > 0.6)
y = Op @ xtrue + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(n)

sigma = 0.1
tau = 1.0
target = tau * sigma * np.sqrt(n)
NITER = 2000


def solve(damp):
    x = pylops.optimization.basic.lsqr(Op, y, damp=damp, niter=NITER,
                                       atol=1e-12, btol=1e-12)[0]
    return x, np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x)


def rel_err(x):
    return np.linalg.norm(x - xtrue) / np.linalg.norm(xtrue)


# --- 1) coarse log sweep -----------------------------------------------------
damps = np.logspace(-4, 1, 26)
res = []
print(f"target residual  tau*sigma*sqrt(n) = {target:.4f}")
print(f"{'damp':>10s} {'||r||':>10s} {'||r||/target':>13s} {'relerr(info)':>13s}")
for d in damps:
    x, r = solve(d)
    res.append(r)
    print(f"{d:10.2e} {r:10.4f} {r / target:13.3f} {rel_err(x):13.3f}")
res = np.array(res)

# --- 2) bracket the crossing and refine by bisection in log(damp) ------------
idx = np.where((res[:-1] - target) * (res[1:] - target) <= 0)[0]
if len(idx) == 0:
    raise RuntimeError("Target residual not bracketed; widen the damp range.")
lo, hi = np.log10(damps[idx[0]]), np.log10(damps[idx[0] + 1])
for _ in range(40):
    mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    _, r = solve(10 ** mid)
    if r < target:
        lo = mid
    else:
        hi = mid
damp_dp = 10 ** (0.5 * (lo + hi))
x_dp, r_dp = solve(damp_dp)

# --- 3) sanity check against the exact Tikhonov solution via SVD ------------
U, S, Vt = np.linalg.svd(K)
x_svd = Vt.T @ (S / (S ** 2 + damp_dp ** 2) * (U.T @ y))
x_old, r_old = solve(0.01)

print()
print(f"discrepancy damp           = {damp_dp:.4g}")
print(f"residual at chosen damp    = {r_dp:.4f} (target {target:.4f})")
print(f"lsqr vs exact SVD mismatch = "
      f"{np.linalg.norm(x_dp - x_svd) / np.linalg.norm(x_svd):.2e}")
print(f"damp=0.01   : ||r||={r_old:.4f} ({r_old / target:.2f}x target), "
      f"relerr={rel_err(x_old):.3f}")
print(f"damp={damp_dp:.3g}: ||r||={r_dp:.4f} ({r_dp / target:.2f}x target), "
      f"relerr={rel_err(x_dp):.3f}")
# (relerr uses xtrue and is only reported for information; it was NOT used
#  to select damp, since xtrue is unknown in a real problem.)
print(f"DAMP_CHOSEN={damp_dp:.4g}")

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
I wrote and ran `sweep.py`. I recommend **`damp ≈ 0.28`** (last line printed: `DAMP_CHOSEN=0.2809`).

**Method: Morozov's discrepancy principle.** `lsqr` with `damp` minimises `||y − Kx||² + damp²·||x||²`. If the noise is white with standard deviation σ, its norm is about `σ·√n = 0.1·√120 ≈ 1.095`. A model that is consistent with the data, but no more, should leave a residual of roughly that size. So you pick the `damp` where `||y − K x_damp|| = σ√n`:

- If the residual is smaller than that, the model is fitting the noise.
- If it is larger, the model is over-smoothed and has lost real signal.

The residual increases steadily as `damp` increases. The script sweeps `damp` over a log grid from 1e-4 to 10, finds the interval where the residual crosses the target, and narrows it down by bisection in log(`damp`). Choosing `damp` this way only needs σ, not `xtrue`.

**Results:**

| damp | residual | residual / target | rel. error vs `xtrue`* |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.01 (your choice) | 0.83 | 0.76 | **1.05** |
| 0.28 (discrepancy) | 1.095 | 1.00 | **0.145** |
| best on the grid (~0.16) | 0.90 | 0.82 | 0.126 |

\*The error against `xtrue` is only a check that works because this is a synthetic test. The selection doesn't use it.

**Why your model looks noisy:** with `damp=0.01` the residual is well below the noise level, so the model is fitting noise. The kernel is a strong smoother, so small singular values blow that noise up, and the error is larger than the signal itself (rel. err ≈ 1.05). With `damp ≈ 0.28` the error drops about 7×.

**Caveats:**
- The discrepancy principle tends to over-smooth slightly. Here it lands just past the error minimum (0.145 vs 0.126). Some people use a safety factor τ slightly above 1 (e.g. 1.01–1.1) when σ is only estimated. Since you know σ exactly, τ = 1 is fine, and it's a variable in the script.
- I tightened `atol`/`btol` so each `lsqr` solve is fully converged. Otherwise stopping the iterations early acts as a second, hidden form of regularization.
- The jump at s = 0.6 will always be smeared with an `||x||²` penalty. If keeping that edge sharp matters, the next step would be a TV or other edge-preserving regularizer, rather than tuning `damp` further.

Op x||^2 + damp^2 ||x||^2.\nWith known noise std sigma, a solution that is consistent with the noise\nshould leave a residual of about the noise norm:\n    ||y - Op x_damp||  ~=  tau * sigma * sqrt(n)      (tau = 1 here)\nThe residual grows monotonically with damp, so we sweep damp on a log grid,\nthen refine the crossing by bisection in log(damp).\n\"\"\"\nimport numpy as np\nimport pylops\n\nrng = np.random.default_rng(7)\nn = 120\ns = np.linspace(0, 1, n)\nK = np.exp(-((s[:, None] - s[None, :]) ** 2) / (2 * 0.04 ** 2)) / n * 10\nOp = pylops.MatrixMult(K)\nxtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2 * s) + 0.5 * (s > 0.6)\ny = Op @ xtrue + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(n)\n\nsigma = 0.1\ntau = 1.0\ntarget = tau * sigma * np.sqrt(n)  # expected noise norm\n\n\ndef solve(damp):\n    x = pylops.optimization.basic.lsqr(\n        Op, y, damp=damp, niter=2000, atol=1e-12, btol=1e-12\n    )[0]\n    res = np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x)\n    err = np.linalg.norm(x - xtrue) / np.linalg.norm(xtrue)\n    return x, res, err\n\n\nprint(f\"target residual tau*sigma*sqrt(n) = {target:.4f}\")\nprint(f\"{'damp':>10} {'||y-Ax||':>10} {'res/target':>10} {'rel.err*':>10}\")\ndamps = np.logspace(-4, 1, 26)\nres_list = []\nfor d in damps:\n    _, r, e = solve(d)\n    res_list.append(r)\n    print(f\"{d:10.4g} {r:10.4f} {r / target:10.3f} {e:10.4f}\")\nres_list = np.array(res_list)\n\n# bracket the crossing and refine by bisection in log(damp)\nidx = np.where(res_list >= target)[0][0]\nlo, hi = np.log10(damps[idx - I recommend **`damp ≈ 0.28`** (last line printed: `DAMP_CHOSEN=0.2809`).\n\n**Method: Morozov's discrepancy principle.** `lsqr` with `damp` minimises `||y − Kx||² + damp²·||x||²`. If the noise is white with standard deviation σ, its norm is about `σ·√n = 0.1·√120 ≈ 1.095`. A model that is consistent with the data, but no more, should leave a residual of roughly that size. So you pick the `damp` where `||y − K x_damp|| = σ√n`:\n\n- If the residual is smaller than that, the model is fitting the noise.\n- If it is larger, the model is over-smoothed and has lost real signal.\n\nThe residual increases steadily as `damp` increases. The script sweeps `damp` over a log grid from 1e-4 to 10, finds the interval where the residual crosses the target, and narrows it down by bisection in log(`damp`). Choosing `damp` this way only needs σ, not `xtrue`.\n\n**Results:**\n\n| damp | residual | residual / target | rel. error vs `xtrue`* |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 0.01 (your choice) | 0.83 | 0.76 | **1.05** |\n| 0.28 (discrepancy) | 1.095 | 1.00 | **0.145** |\n| best on the grid (~0.16) | 0.90 | 0.82 | 0.126 |\n\n\\*The error against `xtrue` is only a check that works because this is a synthetic test. The selection doesn't use it.\n\n**Why your model looks noisy:** with `damp=0.01` the residual is well below the noise level, so the model is fitting noise. The kernel is a strong smoother, so small singular values blow that noise up, and the error is larger than the signal itself (rel. err ≈ 1.05). With `damp ≈ 0.28` the error drops about 7×.\n\n**Caveats:**\n- The discrepancy principle tends to over-smooth slightly. Here it lands just past the error minimum (0.145 vs 0.126). Some people use a safety factor τ slightly above 1 (e.g. 1.01–1.1) when σ is only estimated. """Choose the lsqr damping parameter with Morozov's discrepancy principle.

lsqr with `damp` minimises  ||y - Op x||^2 + damp^2 ||x||^2.
With known noise std sigma, a solution that is consistent with the noise
should leave a residual of about the noise norm:
    ||y - Op x_damp||  ~=  tau * sigma * sqrt(n)      (tau = 1 here)
The residual grows monotonically with damp, so we sweep damp on a log grid,
then refine the crossing by bisection in log(damp).
"""
import numpy as np
import pylops

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
n = 120
s = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
K = np.exp(-((s[:, None] - s[None, :]) ** 2) / (2 * 0.04 ** 2)) / n * 10
Op = pylops.MatrixMult(K)
xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2 * s) + 0.5 * (s > 0.6)
y = Op @ xtrue + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(n)

sigma = 0.1
tau = 1.0
target = tau * sigma * np.sqrt(n)  # expected noise norm


def solve(damp):
    x = pylops.optimization.basic.lsqr(
        Op, y, damp=damp, niter=2000, atol=1e-12, btol=1e-12
    )[0]
    res = np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x)
    err = np.linalg.norm(x - xtrue) / np.linalg.norm(xtrue)
    return x, res, err


print(f"target residual tau*sigma*sqrt(n) = {target:.4f}")
print(f"{'damp':>10} {'||y-Ax||':>10} {'res/target':>10} {'rel.err*':>10}")
damps = np.logspace(-4, 1, 26)
res_list = []
for d in damps:
    _, r, e = solve(d)
    res_list.append(r)
    print(f"{d:10.4g} {r:10.4f} {r / target:10.3f} {e:10.4f}")
res_list = np.array(res_list)

# bracket the crossing and refine by bisection in log(damp)
idx = np.where(res_list >= target)[0][0]
lo, hi = np.log10(damps[idx - 1]), np.log10(damps[idx])
for _ in range(40):
    mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
    _, r, _ = solve(10 ** mid)
    if r < target:
        lo = mid
    else:
        hi = mid
damp_chosen = 10 ** (0.5 * (lo + hi))

_, r_old, e_old = solve(0.01)
_, r_new, e_new = solve(damp_chosen)
print()
print(f"damp=0.01 (trial & error): residual={r_old:.4f} "
      f"({r_old / target:.2f}x target) rel.err={e_old:.4f}")
print(f"damp={damp_chosen:.4g} (discrepancy): residual={r_new:.4f} "
      f"({r_new / target:.2f}x target) rel.err={e_new:.4f}")
print("* rel.err uses xtrue; shown only as a check, NOT used for the choice.")
print(f"DAMP_CHOSEN={damp_chosen:.4g}")

Prompt

I am inverting a smoothing integral operator with lsqr and a damping term. I know the noise standard deviation is exactly 0.1, and I picked damp=0.01 by trial and error, but the model looks noisy. How should I choose damp in a principled way? The synthetic test is:

import numpy as np
import pylops

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
n = 120
s = np.linspace(0, 1, n)
K = np.exp(-((s[:, None] - s[None, :]) ** 2) / (2 * 0.04 ** 2)) / n * 10
Op = pylops.MatrixMult(K)
xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2 * s) + 0.5 * (s > 0.6)
y = Op @ xtrue + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(n)

xinv = pylops.optimization.basic.lsqr(Op, y, damp=0.01, niter=2000)[0]

Please write a runnable Python script saved as sweep.py in the current folder, run it, and tell me what you chose and why. The script must print, as its last line, DAMP_CHOSEN=<value> with the value you recommend.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
I recommend **`eps ≈ 0.18`**. I wrote `sweep.py`, ran it, and its last line is `EPS_CHOSEN=0.1806`. It also saves `sweep.png`, which shows residual vs eps, SNR vs eps, the L-curve, and the true model next to the chosen, over- and under-regularised models.

**Why `eps=5.0` gives all zeros**

PyLops' `fista` uses a soft threshold of `eps·alpha/2`. The model is therefore exactly zero for any `eps ≥ 2·max|Aᵀy|`, which is **4.28** for your data. `eps=5.0` is above that, so every coefficient gets thresholded away. Compute that cutoff first and treat it as the top of your search range.

**How I chose `eps`**

- **Grid:** 41 values, log-spaced from 4.28 down to 4.3e-5 (five orders of magnitude). Each solve runs `niter=2000` and starts from the previous solution. A check that started from zero instead gave the same answers in the useful range (relative difference about 1e-10 to 1e-5).
- **Main criterion: discrepancy principle.** You know the noise level, so the best regularisation is the strongest one that still fits the data to the noise level: `‖y − Ax‖ ≤ σ√M = 0.05·√80 = 0.447`. The largest `eps` that meets this is **0.18**, with residual 0.419 and an SNR of 20.8 dB against the true model.
- **Check against the true model (synthetic only):** the best SNR is at `eps ≈ 0.10` (21.8 dB), only about 1 dB better and in the same range. This check isn't available on real data, but it shows the discrepancy pick is close to the best.
- **L-curve: not useful here.** Its automatic corner lands at 5.7e-5, at the noise-fitting end of the curve. With an L1 penalty this curve has no clear corner, so I ignored it.

**What each range of `eps` does**

| eps | Result |
|---|---|
| 0.4 to 4.3 | Under-fits: the model shrinks too much (SNR 16 dB or lower) |
| 0.1 to 0.2 | Best range: all 6 spikes recovered with nearly the right amplitudes |
| below 0.05 | Fits the noise: 60 to 78 nonzero values, SNR falls to about 17 dB |

At 0.18, about 15 coefficients are above 1e-3 against 6 true spikes. The extras are small leftovers from the soft threshold. If you need exactly 6 spikes, add a hard threshold or a least-squares refit on the detected spikes afterwards.

**The line to change in your script:**

```python
xinv = pylops.optimization.sparsity.fista(Op, y, eps=0.18, niter=500)[0]
```

I only checked that the sweep converged at `niter=2000`. Re-check your result at 500 iterations or raise `niter`.

On real data, keep this method: set the top of the range to `2·max|Opᴴy|`, sweep downwards, and pick the largest `eps` whose residual is at or below `σ·√M`.

"""Choose `eps` for pylops fista with a log-spaced sweep.

Criteria:
  * discrepancy principle (noise std known): largest eps with
    ||y - Op x|| <= tau * sigma * sqrt(M)   -> recommended
  * best SNR vs the true model (synthetic only, for reference)
  * L-curve corner (log ||x||_1 vs log ||y - Op x||), for reference
"""

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

import pylops
from pylops.utils.metrics import snr

# ---------------- problem (as given) ----------------
rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
N, M = 200, 80
A = rng.standard_normal((M, N)) / np.sqrt(M)
Op = pylops.MatrixMult(A)
xtrue = np.zeros(N)
xtrue[rng.choice(N, 6, replace=False)] = rng.uniform(1, 3, 6) * rng.choice([-1, 1], 6)
sigma = 0.05
y = Op @ xtrue + sigma * rng.standard_normal(M)

NITER = 2000  # enough for each solve to converge (checked below)
TAU = 1.0


def solve(eps, x0=None):
    return pylops.optimization.sparsity.fista(
        Op, y, x0=x0, eps=eps, niter=NITER, tol=1e-12
    )[0]


# ---------------- scale-based grid ----------------
# PyLops fista thresholds with eps*alpha/2, i.e. it minimises
# 1/2||y-Ax||^2 + eps/2 ||x||_1  ->  x = 0 for every eps >= 2*max|A^T y|.
eps_max = 2 * np.max(np.abs(Op.H @ y))
print(f"eps above which x = 0 : {eps_max:.4f}  (you used eps=5.0)")
epsilons = eps_max * np.logspace(0, -5, 41)  # large -> small, warm start

rnorm, l1norm, snrs, nnz = [], [], [], []
xs = []
x0 = None
for eps in epsilons:
    x = solve(eps, x0)
    x0 = x.copy()
    xs.append(x)
    rnorm.append(np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x))
    l1norm.append(np.sum(np.abs(x)))
    snrs.append(snr(xtrue, x))
    nnz.append(np.sum(np.abs(x) > 1e-3))
rnorm, l1norm, snrs, nnz = map(np.array, (rnorm, l1norm, snrs, nnz))

# convergence check: cold start vs warm start at a few eps
for i in (10, 20, 30):
    xc = solve(epsilons[i])
    print(f"  converged check eps={epsilons[i]:.2e}: "
          f"||x_cold - x_warm||/||x|| = "
          f"{np.linalg.norm(xc - xs[i]) / max(np.linalg.norm(xs[i]), 1e-12):.1e}")

print(f"\n{'eps':>10} {'||r||':>9} {'||x||_1':>9} {'nnz':>4} {'SNR(dB)':>8}")
for e, r, l, k, s in zip(epsilons, rnorm, l1norm, nnz, snrs):
    print(f"{e:10.4g} {r:9.4f} {l:9.3f} {k:4d} {s:8.2f}")

# ---------------- criteria ----------------
target = TAU * sigma * np.sqrt(M)
ok = np.where(rnorm <= target)[0]
i_dp = ok[0]  # epsilons are decreasing -> first ok is the largest eps
i_snr = int(np.argmax(snrs))

# L-curve corner (curvature in log-log, increasing eps order)
mask = l1norm > 0
e_, r_, x_ = epsilons[mask][::-1], rnorm[mask][::-1], l1norm[mask][::-1]
lr, lx = np.log(r_), np.log(x_)
s = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(np.hypot(np.diff(lr), np.diff(lx)))])
dr, dx = np.gradient(lr, s), np.gradient(lx, s)
ddr, ddx = np.gradient(dr, s), np.gradient(dx, s)
kappa = (dr * ddx - ddr * dx) / (dr**2 + dx**2) ** 1.5
kappa[[0, -1]] = -np.inf
eps_lc = e_[int(np.argmax(kappa))]

print(f"\nDiscrepancy target tau*sigma*sqrt(M) = {target:.4f}")
print(f"Discrepancy principle : eps = {epsilons[i_dp]:.4g} "
      f"(||r||={rnorm[i_dp]:.4f}, SNR={snrs[i_dp]:.2f} dB, nnz={nnz[i_dp]})")
print(f"Best SNR (synthetic)  : eps = {epsilons[i_snr]:.4g} "
      f"(||r||={rnorm[i_snr]:.4f}, SNR={snrs[i_snr]:.2f} dB, nnz={nnz[i_snr]})")
print(f"L-curve corner        : eps = {eps_lc:.4g}")

# ---------------- plots ----------------
fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(11, 8))
ax = axs[0, 0]
ax.loglog(epsilons, rnorm, "k.-")
ax.axhline(target, color="r", ls="--", label="tau*sigma*sqrt(M)")
ax.axvline(epsilons[i_dp], color="r", label="discrepancy")
ax.set(xlabel="eps", ylabel="||y - Op x||", title="Residual vs eps")
ax.legend()
ax = axs[0, 1]
ax.semilogx(epsilons, snrs, "k.-")
ax.axvline(epsilons[i_dp], color="r", label="discrepancy")
ax.axvline(epsilons[i_snr], color="b", ls=":", label="best SNR")
ax.set(xlabel="eps", ylabel="SNR (dB)", title="SNR vs eps (synthetic only)")
ax.legend()
ax = axs[1, 0]
ax.loglog(rnorm[mask], l1norm[mask], "k.-")
ax.loglog(rnorm[i_dp], l1norm[i_dp], "ro", label="discrepancy")
ax.set(xlabel="||y - Op x||", ylabel="||x||_1", title="L-curve")
ax.legend()
ax = axs[1, 1]
i_over = max(i_dp - 6, 0)
i_under = min(i_dp + 12, len(epsilons) - 1)
ax.stem(xtrue, linefmt="k-", markerfmt="ko", basefmt=" ", label="true")
ax.plot(xs[i_dp], "r.", label=f"chosen eps={epsilons[i_dp]:.3g}")
ax.plot(xs[i_over], "g+", label=f"over eps={epsilons[i_over]:.3g}")
ax.plot(xs[i_under], "bx", ms=4, label=f"under eps={epsilons[i_under]:.3g}")
ax.set(title="Models")
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("sweep.png", dpi=110)
print("Saved sweep.png")

print(f"EPS_CHOSEN={epsilons[i_dp]:.4g}")

For\n   `spgl1`, this is exactly `sigma = τ σ sqrt(N)`.\n2. **Synthetic with a true model**: maximise `pylops.utils.metrics.snr(xtrue, x)`\n   (report it, but warn it does not transfer 1:1 to field data).\n3. **Nothing known**: **L-curve** - plot `log ‖Rx‖` vs `log ‖y − Op x‖` and pick the\n   point of maximum curvature. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019wS53Qwmq52ERnrS2UjiPC","type":"tool_result","content":"2.8.0\n(Op: 'LinearOperator', y: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.number]], x0: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.number]] | None = None, niter: int = 10, SOp: Optional[ForwardRef('LinearOperator')] = None, eps: float = 0.1, alpha: float | None = None, eigsdict: dict[str, typing.Any] | None = None, tol: float = 1e-10, rtol: float = 0.0, rtol1: float = 0.0, threshkind: Literal['hard', 'soft', 'half', 'hard-percentile', 'soft-percentile', 'half-percentile'] = 'soft', perc: float | None = None, decay: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.number]] | None = None, monitorres: bool = False, show: bool = False, itershow: tuple[int, int, int] = (10, 10, 10), callback: collections.abc.Callable | None = None, preallocate: bool = False) -> tuple[numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.number]], int, numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.number]]]\n\"\"\"Template for choosing a regularisation weight in a PyLops inversion.\n\nRuns as-is on a toy 1-D deconvolution with second-derivative (smoothness)\nregularisation. To adapt it, replace ``build_problem`` and ``solve`` and keep\nthe sweep, the selection criteria and the plots.\n\nCriteria implemented:\n- L-curve corner (maximum curvature in log-log);\n- discrepancy principle (needs the noise standard deviation);\n- best SNR against a known model (synthetic tests only);\n- GCV, exact on dense matrices (small quadratic problems only).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\n\nimport pylops\nfrom pylops.utils.metrics import snr\n\n\ndef build_problem(rng):\n    \"\"\"ADAPT: return (Op, Reg, y, xtrue or None, noise_std or None).\"\"\"\n    nt = 201\n    t = np.arange(nt) * 0.004\n    h, _, hcenter = pylops.utils.wavelets.ricker(t[:41], f0=15)\n    Op = pylops.signalprocessing.Convolve1D(nt, h=h, offset=hcenter)\n    Reg = pylops.SecondDerivative(nt)\n\n    xtrue = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 3 * t) * np.exp(-t)  # smooth model\n    noise_std = 0.05\n    y = Op @ xtrue + noise_std * rng.standard_normal(nt)\n    return Op, Reg, y, xtrue, noise_std\n\n\ndef solve(Op, Reg, y, eps, x0):\n    \"\"\"ADAPT: the user's solver call with everything but ``eps`` fixed.\"\"\"\n    Opaug = pylops.VStack([Op, eps * Reg])\n    yaug = np.concatenate([y, np.zeros(Reg.shape[0])])\n    return pylops.cgls(Opaug, yaug, x0=x0, niter=200, tol=1e-10)[0]\n\n\ndef lcurve_corner(epsilons, rnorm, xnorm):\n    \"\"\"Index of the L-curve corner (maximum curvature in log-log).\n\n    Points are ordered by increasing eps so that the corner between the\n    \"under-regularised\" (vertical) and \"over-regularised\" (horizontal) branches\n    has positive curvature. A second knee with opposite curvature can appear\n    at very large eps (model pushed into the null space of the regulariser):\n    it is not the L-curve corner.\n    \"\"\"\n    order = np.argsort(epsilons)\n    lr, lx = np.log(rnorm[order]), np.log(xnorm[order])\n    # parametrise by arc length to make finite differences uniform\n    s = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(np.hypot(np.diff(lr), np.diff(lx)))])\n    dr, dx = np.gradient(lr, s), np.gradient(lx, s)\n    ddr, ddx = np.gradient(dr, s), np.gradient(dx, s)\n    kappa = (dr * ddx - ddr * dx) / (dr**2 + dx**2) ** 1.5\n    kappa[[0, -1]] = -np.inf  # ends are not valid corners\n    kappa_orig = np.empty_like(kappa)\n    kappa_orig[order] = kappa","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f56a55f8-2e99-4508-b2d1-ceff2678c910","uuid":"30d9555e-9314-4e13-9561-53a14bfe9e91","timestamp":"2026-11-01T20:36:42.641Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"2.8.0\n(Op: 'LinearOperator', y: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.number]], x0: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.number]] | None = None, niter: int = 10, SOp: Optional[ForwardRef('LinearOperator')] = None, eps: float = 0.1, alpha: float | None = None, eigsdict: dict[str, typing.Any] | None = None, tol: float = 1e-10, rtol: float = 0.0, rtol1: float = 0.0, threshkind: Literal['hard', 'soft', 'half', 'hard-percentile', 'soft-percentile', 'half-percentile'] = 'soft', perc: float | None = None, decay: numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[numpy.number]] | None = None, monitorres: bool = False, show: bool = False, itershow: tuple[int, int, int] = (10, 10, 10), callback: collections.abc.Callable | None = None, preallocate: bool = False) -> tuple[numpy.ndarray[typing.Any, numpy.dtype[num

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
I recommend **`eps ≈ 0.18`**. The script is `sweep.py` and it ends with `EPS_CHOSEN=0.1806`. It ran successfully and saved a plot to `sweep_eps.png`.

## Why `eps=5.0` returns all zeros
PyLops' `fista` minimises `‖y − Op x‖² + eps‖x‖₁`. Whenever `eps ≥ 2·max|Opᴴ y|`, the exact solution is `x = 0`. In your problem that threshold is **4.28**, so `eps=5.0` is above it and the zeros are correct, not a solver failure. Use this threshold as the top of any `eps` search.

## How I chose `eps`
The script tries 41 log-spaced values from 4.28 down to 4.28e-5. Each run keeps `niter=500` and starts from the previous solution. I re-ran a few values from scratch with 2000 iterations to check convergence. At the chosen `eps` the two results agree to about 1e-10. At much smaller `eps` (5,000 to 20,000 times below 4.28) they differ by 1–2%, which doesn't affect the choice.

| Criterion | eps | Residual | SNR vs true model |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Discrepancy principle** (chosen) | **0.181** | 0.419 (target 0.470) | 20.8 dB |
| Best SNR against the true model | 0.102 | 0.319 | 21.8 dB |
| L-curve | no clear corner | – | – |

- **Discrepancy principle:** because you know the noise standard deviation (σ = 0.05), I picked the largest `eps` whose data misfit is still at the noise level: `‖y − Op x‖ ≤ 1.05·σ·√M ≈ 0.47`. That is **eps = 0.18**. It recovers all six spikes with correct signs and close amplitudes. It also leaves some tiny non-zero values: 15 entries are above 1e-3.
- **Comparison with the true model:** I can only compute this because your test problem is synthetic. It peaks at eps ≈ 0.10, only 1 dB better than 0.18, so the noise-based pick is close to the best possible. On real data you won't have this check, but you will still have σ.
- **L-curve:** the curve of `‖x‖₁` against the residual bends smoothly with no sharp corner, which is common with an L1 penalty. The automatic corner pick went to the smallest `eps` on the grid, which is meaningless, so I ignored it.

The plot shows the L-curve, the residual against `eps` with the noise target, the SNR against `eps`, and the model at the chosen `eps` next to one with too much and one with too little regularisation.

## Change to your script
```python
xinv = pylops.optimization.sparsity.fista(Op, y, eps=0.18, niter=500)[0]
```

If you want fewer leftover small values, `eps` between 0.1 and 0.25 is a safe range. For new data, rerun `sweep.py` with the real noise level. A quick rule for that data is to start near `0.04 × 2·max|Opᴴ y|` and refine with the noise-level target.

"""Choose `eps` for pylops fista with a sweep: discrepancy principle (noise std known),
L-curve, and SNR against the true model (available only because this is a synthetic).

PyLops fista minimises  ||y - Op x||_2^2 + eps ||x||_1  (soft threshold = eps*alpha/2),
so x = 0 is the solution whenever eps >= eps_max = 2 * max|Op^H y|.
"""
import numpy as np
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pylops
from pylops.optimization.sparsity import fista
from pylops.utils.metrics import snr

# ---------------- problem (as given) ----------------
rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
N, M = 200, 80
A = rng.standard_normal((M, N)) / np.sqrt(M)
Op = pylops.MatrixMult(A)
xtrue = np.zeros(N)
xtrue[rng.choice(N, 6, replace=False)] = rng.uniform(1, 3, 6) * rng.choice([-1, 1], 6)
sigma = 0.05
y = Op @ xtrue + sigma * rng.standard_normal(M)

NITER = 500
TAU = 1.05  # discrepancy safety factor


def solve(eps, x0=None):
    return fista(Op, y, x0=x0, eps=eps, niter=NITER, tol=1e-12)[0]


# ---------------- scale-based grid ----------------
eps_max = 2 * np.max(np.abs(Op.H @ y))  # above this, fista returns all zeros
print(f"eps_max (all-zero threshold) = 2*max|Op^H y| = {eps_max:.4f}")
print(f"your eps = 5.0 is {5.0 / eps_max:.1f}x eps_max -> x = 0")
epss = eps_max * np.logspace(0, -5, 41)  # large -> small, warm start

res, l1, snrs, xs = [], [], [], []
x0 = None
for eps in epss:
    x = solve(eps, x0)
    x0 = x
    xs.append(x)
    res.append(np.linalg.norm(y - Op @ x))
    l1.append(np.sum(np.abs(x)))
    snrs.append(snr(xtrue, x) if np.any(x) else -np.inf)
res, l1, snrs = map(np.array, (res, l1, snrs))

# convergence sanity check: re-solve a few values cold with 4x iterations
for i in (10, 25, 35):
    xc = fista(Op, y, eps=epss[i], niter=4 * NITER, tol=1e-12)[0]
    print(f"  conv. check eps={epss[i]:.2e}: rel. diff warm(500) vs cold(2000) = "
          f"{np.linalg.norm(xc - xs[i]) / max(np.linalg.norm(xc), 1e-12):.1e}")

# ---------------- criteria ----------------
target = TAU * sigma * np.sqrt(M)
ok = np.where(res <= target)[0]
i_disc = ok[0]  # largest eps (grid sorted descending) meeting the discrepancy
eps_disc = epss[i_disc]

# L-curve: log residual vs log L1 norm, max curvature (only where x != 0)
nz = l1 > 0
lr, lx, le = np.log(res[nz]), np.log(l1[nz]), np.log(epss[nz])
dr, dx = np.gradient(lr, le), np.gradient(lx, le)
ddr, ddx = np.gradient(dr, le), np.gradient(dx, le)
kappa = (dr * ddx - ddr * dx) / (dr ** 2 + dx ** 2) ** 1.5
i_lc = np.argmax(kappa)
eps_lc = epss[nz][i_lc]

i_snr = np.argmax(snrs)
eps_snr = epss[i_snr]

print(f"\nswept {len(epss)} eps values in [{epss[-1]:.2e}, {epss[0]:.2e}], niter={NITER}")
print(f"discrepancy target tau*sigma*sqrt(M) = {target:.4f}")
for name, i, e in [("discrepancy", i_disc, eps_disc),
                   ("L-curve", np.where(nz)[0][i_lc], eps_lc),
                   ("max SNR (oracle)", i_snr, eps_snr)]:
    print(f"  {name:17s}: eps={e:.3g}  residual={res[i]:.4f}  SNR={snrs[i]:.1f} dB  "
          f"nnz={np.sum(np.abs(xs[i]) > 1e-3)}")

# ---------------- plots ----------------
fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 8))
axs[0, 0].loglog(res[nz], l1[nz], ".-")
axs[0, 0].loglog(res[i_disc], l1[i_disc], "ro", label="discrepancy")
axs[0, 0].loglog(res[nz][i_lc], l1[nz][i_lc], "gs", mfc="none", label="L-curve corner")
axs[0, 0].set(xlabel="||y - Op x||", ylabel="||x||_1", title="L-curve")
axs[0, 0].legend()
axs[0, 1].loglog(epss, res, ".-", label="residual")
axs[0, 1].axhline(target, color="r", ls="--", label="tau sigma sqrt(M)")
axs[0, 1].axvline(eps_disc, color="r")
axs[0, 1].set(xlabel="eps", ylabel="||y - Op x||", title="Residual vs eps")
axs[0, 1].legend()
axs[1, 0].semilogx(epss, snrs, ".-")
axs[1, 0].axvline(eps_disc, color="r", label="discrepancy")
axs[1, 0].axvline(eps_snr, color="k", ls=":", label="max SNR")
axs[1, 0].set(xlabel="eps", ylabel="SNR [dB]", title="SNR vs eps (synthetic only)")
axs[1, 0].legend()
i_over = max(i_disc - 8, 0)
i_under = min(i_disc + 12, len(epss) - 1)
axs[1, 1].plot(xtrue, "k", lw=3, label="true")
axs[1, 1].plot(xs[i_over], "b", label=f"over-reg eps={epss[i_over]:.2g}")
axs[1, 1].plot(xs[i_disc], "r--", label=f"chosen eps={eps_disc:.2g}")
axs[1, 1].plot(xs[i_under], "g", alpha=0.6, label=f"under-reg eps={epss[i_under]:.2g}")
axs[1, 1].set(title="Models")
axs[1, 1].legend(fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("sweep_eps.png", dpi=120)
print("plot saved to sweep_eps.png")

print(f"EPS_CHOSEN={eps_disc:.4g}")

Do not\nlaunch a full grid over several parameters unless the problem is small.\n\n## 2. Pick the criterion\n\nChoose based on what the user knows:\n\n1. **Known noise level** (sigma per sample, or an estimate from a noise-only\n   window): **discrepancy principle** - choose the largest regularisation whose\n   data residual `‖y − Op x‖` is ≤ `τ · σ · sqrt(N)`, `τ ≈ 1.0–1.1`. For\n   `spgl1`, this is exactly `sigma = τ σ sqrt(N)`.\n2. **Synthetic with a true model**: maximise `pylops.utils.metrics.snr(xtrue, x)`\n   (report it, but warn it does not transfer 1:1 to field data).\n3. **Nothing known**: **L-curve** - plot `log ‖Rx‖` vs `log ‖y − Op x‖` and pick the\n   point of maximum curvature. Needs a wide enough range to show both branches.\n4. **Small problem** (`Op.todense()` affordable, N, M ≲ 3000) and quadratic\n   regularisation: **GCV** computed exactly on the dense matrices (implemented in\n   the template).\n\nReport more than one criterion when they are cheap; disagreement between them is\ninformation for the user.\n\n## 3. With derivative regularisers a second knee often appears at\nvery large ε (the model collapses into the null space of `R`, e.g. a linear\ntrend for `SecondDerivative`); it bends the other way and is not the L-curve\ncorner – the template's curvature orientation already excludes it.\n\n## 4.
